content: Have you ever wondered where the crunchy onions in your pav bhaji come from? They don't grow in supermarkets! Let's travel to a small village in Karnataka called Belvanika. Here lives a young boy named Basva, and his family is getting ready for something magical that happens in the soil every July.

Before a farmer can plant a seed, they look at the hard, dry ground. If you try to push a tiny, fragile seed into a rock-hard ground, what do you think would happen? How can we make the soil soft and friendly for the baby plant?

Imagine trying to sleep on a bed made of bricks. Not comfortable, right? Seeds feel the same way! They need a soft, fluffy bed of soil to stretch their roots. To make this bed, Basva's Appa (father) uses a special iron rod to dig and loosen the soil.

content.title: Loosening the Soil
content.description: The Khunti digs into the hard earth, breaking it into soft, crumbly pieces.

content: The iron rod Basva's father uses is called a **Khunti**. It helps to loosen the soil and make it ready for sowing seeds. Sowing is the process of planting seeds in the soil.
Khunti (खूंटी): An iron implement used to dig the soil, loosen it, and make it soft for planting seeds.
Sowing (बुवाई): The act of planting seeds in the earth so they can grow into crops.

Explain to students that the tools have different names in different languages. In Basva's area, they speak Kannada. The iron rod is called a Khunti, but in other states, it might have a different name.

question: Why does Basva's Appa use the Khunti on the field?

content: Think about the potted plants at your home or school. Have you ever seen someone gently poking the soil in the pot with a small stick or trowel? They are doing exactly what Basva's Appa does on a large farm! Why do you think roots need loose soil instead of hard packed dirt?

Once the soil is loose, it's time to sow! But Appa doesn't just throw the seeds everywhere. He uses a **Kurige** pulled by bullocks to drop seeds at the right distance. If seeds are too close, they fight for water and food. If they are too far, land is wasted. This is just like spacing out students during an exam so everyone has enough room!

content.title: The Kurige at Work
content.description: Bullocks pull the Kurige while Appa carefully drops seeds into the funnels.

content: Kurige (कूरिगे): A seed drill pulled by bullocks that drops seeds evenly in rows.
Weeds (खरपतवार): Unwanted plants that grow along with the crops and steal their water and fertilizer.

Mini Challenge: Weeds are unwanted plants that grow next to crops and steal their food. And eventually, the onion plants need to be harvested using an Illige (a sharp tool) when their leaves turn yellow and dry. Ask your parents to show you an onion with its root side and sprout side. Draw a picture of a farm showing the Kurige in action and label it!
Students often think all plants grow at the same speed. Actually, Appa says it takes about 20 days for the onion sprouts to finally pop out of the soil. Farming requires a lot of patience!
